title: Status 'Open' shows as the verb 'திற' (meaning 'open it!') in Tamil
what_happens: In the Take action dialog in Tamil, the status chip next to the severity reads 'திற', the command form of 'open'.
what_should_happen: A status word such as 'திறந்தநிலை' (open status).
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/journey-collector-storm.browser.mjs 3181 (server started without --frozen); see storm-ta-4-act.txt line 195
root_cause_guess: unknown; a one-word string translated with no context

title: Fixed labels on the Tamil Briefing stay in English
what_happens: In Tamil, the Briefing still shows CRITICAL NOW, WATCHFUL, Warnings, Oldest open complaint, First report, 'what each received', 'Written by AI from the records' in English. Headline chips are English too. This server has no AI provider, so the AI translation is off, but these are fixed screen labels that a dictionary should cover.
what_should_happen: Fixed labels are Tamil even with the AI translator off.
root_cause_guess: dictionary gap; page relies on live AI translation (log: '[i18n] AI translation unavailable')

title: Cyclone banner popover stays open on top of the Take action dialog
what_happens: After opening the Cyclone Murasu banner, pressing Act on the severe item opens the dialog, but the banner popover stays on top and hides the incident title and the first steps. Escape did not close it in the run.
what_should_happen: Opening a dialog closes the popover (or the dialog sits above it).
root_cause_guess: popover z-index and no outside-click close; not checked in source

title: 'Severe severity' wording
what_happens: Chip reads 'Severe severity' on the incident card and 'Severe severity incident' on news rows.

title: Raw ISO date '2026-11-07' in the cyclone popover
what_happens: The IMD row ends with 2026-11-07 while other dates read '6 Nov'.
what_should_happen: Same date style as the rest of the page.

title: --frozen server rejects staff sign-in in a real browser
what_happens: With --frozen, a Collector signs in (200) but /collector goes back to /login. Tokens are stamped with the frozen clock (12 h life); the edge middleware checks them with the real clock, a day later. This run used a server without --frozen to get past it.
what_should_happen: Harness note: browser journeys need a clock the middleware agrees with.
repro: start with --frozen --ticking, sign in via the form, load /collector
root_cause_guess: tests/qa/pass4/freeze-clock.cjs patches Node only, not the edge sandbox
